# 5-Day Lisbon Budget Trip Plan

A balanced Lisbon trip for **2 adults** with a **€1,800 total budget** excluding intercontinental flights, designed for walkable neighborhoods, one museum day, one food-focused day, and one relaxed coastal half-day. Dates assumed: **2026-04-10 to 2026-04-14**.

## Day-by-Day Lisbon Itinerary and Budget

| Day | Focus | Area Base | Estimated Cost for 2 | Main Spend |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Day 1 | Old-town arrival and viewpoints | Baixa / Chiado | €210 | Lodging, tram/metro, casual dinner |
| Day 2 | Museum day and central Lisbon | Baixa / Avenida | €245 | Museum tickets, café lunch, dinner |
| Day 3 | Food-focused day | Bairro Alto / Cais do Sodré | €280 | Tastings, market eats, drinks |
| Day 4 | Relaxed coastal half-day | Belém / Alcântara | €235 | Transit, pastries, lunch, light sightseeing |
| Day 5 | Neighborhood stroll and departure | Alfama / Graça | €170 | Breakfast, local transit, snacks |
|  | Buffer for extras | Flexible | €160 | Contingency for taxis, souvenirs, extra meals |

## Balanced 5-Day Plan

### Day 1: Arrival, Baixa, Chiado, and sunset views
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, and do a light walk through **Baixa** and **Rossio**.
- Afternoon: Explore **Chiado** and take the **Santa Justa / Carmo** area on foot.
- Dinner: Simple tascas or petiscos near **Bairro Alto**.
- Estimated cost: **€210** for 2
- Stay area: **Baixa, Chiado, or Cais do Sodré** for the most walkable start.

### Day 2: Museum day in central Lisbon
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Visit **Museu Nacional do Azulejo** or **Calouste Gulbenkian Museum**.
- Afternoon: Slow lunch, then **Príncipe Real** or **Avenida da Liberdade** stroll.
- Dinner: Mid-range Portuguese dinner in central Lisbon.
- Estimated cost: **€245** for 2
- Tip: Pick one museum only so the day stays relaxed and budget-friendly.

### Day 3: Food-focused Lisbon
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- Morning: Coffee and pastel de nata tasting near **Baixa** or **Alfama**.
- Afternoon: Lunch at **Time Out Market** or a traditional market/tasca circuit.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/83/Lobster%2C_Time_Out_Market_Lisboa_%2850661858143%29.jpg Alt=Afternoon: Lunch at **Time Out Market** or a traditional market/tasca circuit, Lisbon, Portugal
- Dinner: Tapas/petiscos crawl in **Cais do Sodré** or **Bairro Alto**.
- Estimated cost: **€280** for 2
- Best fit: This is your highest food-spend day, so keep daytime sightseeing light.

### Day 4: Relaxed coastal half-day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- Morning: Head to **Belém** for a slow riverside/coastal-style half-day.
- Afternoon: See **Belém Tower** area, then linger at cafés and green space.
- Dinner: Return to central Lisbon for an easy neighborhood meal.
- Estimated cost: **€235** for 2
- Transit note: Use tram/rail/ride-hail only if needed; the day works well with a slower pace.

### Day 5: Alfama, Graça, and departure
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg
- Morning: Walk **Alfama** and **Graça** for viewpoints and final photos.
- Afternoon: Last lunch, pickup snacks, and head to the airport.
- Dinner: Not essential unless your departure is late.
- Estimated cost: **€170** for 2
- Best fit: Keep luggage light and use a central base to avoid backtracking.

## Stay Areas That Fit Your Budget and Style

- **Baixa / Chiado**: Best all-around for first-time visitors; very walkable, central, easy transit access.
- **Cais do Sodré**: Good for food, nightlife, and river access; convenient but can be noisier.
- **Alfama / Graça**: Most atmospheric and scenic; best if you like hills and historic streets.
- **Avenida / Saldanha**: Usually better value; still central, slightly less charming but practical.

### Budget lodging target
- Aim for **€120–€180 per night total** for a decent apartment or hotel for 2.
- To stay within budget, prioritize:
  - walking distance to metro/tram
  - breakfast included if available
  - free cancellation
  - elevator if you have heavy luggage, since Lisbon is hilly

## Transit Tips for Lisbon

- Use **metro + walking** as your default; Lisbon is compact but hilly.
- Trams are scenic, but not always the fastest option.
- A **Viva Viagem** card is useful for metro, buses, trams, and some trains.
- For Belém, consider **train or tram + walk** depending on your exact base.
- Use taxis or ride-hail only for late nights, airport transfers, or steep uphill returns.
- Budget for transit at about **€8–€15 per day for 2** if you mostly walk.

## Packing for Mild Spring Weather

- Light jacket or trench coat
- Comfortable walking shoes with grip
- 2–3 breathable layers
- Compact umbrella or packable rain shell
- Sunglasses and sunscreen
- Day bag with water bottle
- Phone charger and power bank
- Slightly dressier outfit for dinners
- Small crossbody or anti-theft day bag
- Reusable tote for snacks, market buys, or laundry

## Budget Check for the Full Trip

- Accommodation: **€600–€900**
- Food and drinks: **€420–€600**
- Local transit: **€50–€90**
- Attractions and museum tickets: **€60–€140**
- Buffer and extras: **€160**
- Total target: **€1,290–€1,890**

Best way to stay under **€1,800**: choose mid-range lodging around **€140–€170/night**, keep one higher-spend food day, and use walking/metro for most movement.

## Quick Actions

- Lisbon tourism overview: https://www.visitlisboa.com/en/
- Lisbon Metro: https://www.metrolisboa.pt/en/
- Calouste Gulbenkian Museum: https://gulbenkian.pt/museu/en/
